chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Ben Webster's drinking: Charlie Shavers and the Philadelphia hotel window
summary: Ben once squared off at Shavers, and in Philadelphia he stuck his head through a hotel window, getting Collins's group thrown out.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: The (inaudible) do you feel that Ben was a very gentle person?

But only when he drank, and he wanted to fight, every -- you know, he wanted to fight, but he never wanted to fight me. I don't know why, and I was around him at this time -- I say at this time, many times when he would drink. But never would he do this. I don't know why. I remember once he squared off at Charlie Shavers, and Charlie Shavers was like a young bull, and Charlie said if you draw at me I'll kill you. And Ben sobered up, this time he didn't hit. But I remember one time we were in-- when I was with Slam we played Philadelphia, and Ben and I were living in the same hotel, and it was snowing and cold as it could be. But after the job we would go to my room and I'd play the guitar, and we had a pianist with us by the name of Beryl Booker, a girl who was a native of Philadelphia.
And she would come up to the hotel, and her friends,

and I would play and they would dance and sing. Well, they had a regular chorus line. So the man, the owner came up and said, look, Mr. Collins, if you keep this noise up, you know, I'm going to have to put you out. You're disturbing the other patrons. I said, okay. Oh, so I said, look, we'll just have to cut this out.
You should have booked the show somewhere (inaudible)

Wait a minute. So we decided to go by Ben's room and see him, so we went by Ben's room and we got in here and Ben wanted to sing, and you know, so he got the girls to do it, to sing again. I wouldn't play, but the noise started again and the man knocked on the door and Ben stood up to say something, man, and he had been drinking. He stuck his head through, right through this plate glass window -- well, not a plate glass window, but the window, and it's snowing outside, the air gusted in, and the man put us all out of the hotel, about five. And cold. And Ben had done it again, you know. But he was just such a beautiful -- I loved him.
